Let \(G=F_2=\langle a,b\rangle\) be the free group on two generators.

**Step 1: Upper bound.**  
\(F_2\) is countable: every element is a finite reduced word in \(a,a^{-1},b,b^{-1}\). Hence the set of subgroups of \(F_2\) is a subset of the power set \(\mathcal P(F_2)\), so

\[
|\operatorname{Sub}(F_2)|\le 2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

**Step 2: Lower bound.**  
Consider the homomorphism

\[
\phi:F_2\to \mathbb Z,\qquad \phi(a)=1,\ \phi(b)=0.
\]

Let \(K=\ker \phi\). The cosets of \(K\) are represented by \(a^n\) for \(n\in\mathbb Z\). By the Reidemeister–Schreier method, \(K\) is a free group with free basis

\[
c_n=a^n b a^{-n}\qquad (n\in\mathbb Z).
\]

Thus \(K\le F_2\) is a free group of countably infinite rank.

Now for each subset \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z\), define

\[
H_S=\langle c_n : n\in S\rangle \le K \le F_2.
\]

If \(S\neq T\), say \(n\in S\setminus T\), then \(c_n\in H_S\). But \(c_n\) cannot lie in \(H_T\), because in the free basis \(\{c_m:m\in\mathbb Z\}\), the element \(c_n\) has normal form using the letter \(c_n\), while every element of \(H_T\) uses only letters \(c_m\) with \(m\in T\). Hence \(H_S\neq H_T\).

There are \(2^{\aleph_0}\) subsets \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z\), so \(F_2\) has at least \(2^{\aleph_0}\) subgroups.

Combining the upper and lower bounds,

\[
|\operatorname{Sub}(F_2)|=2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

\[
\boxed{2^{\aleph_0}}
\]
